lens: evidence integrity, privacy, identity, and action authority

findings.criterion: Deployed temporal ambiguity and action authority
findings.observation: The frozen local build keeps seeded Wednesday and Tuesday-afternoon statements unresolved and creates no time action. The live public Demo still shows four confirmable items, zero clarification items, and a meeting proposal from unresolved Tuesday afternoon.
findings.evidence: output/playwright/2026-08-11-ui99-production-demo-002.png; Playwright session ts-99-live-002; DEMO-06 and DEMO-07 in docs/evaluations/2026-08-11-system-ui-click-acceptance-003.json.
findings.user_impact: The deployed evaluation surface still teaches users that ambiguous relative time can become relationship state or scheduling authority.
findings.recommendation: Keep the paid gate blocked until the guarded build is deployed and an automated production probe asserts the exact ambiguity outcome.
findings.verification: The live seeded note produces two supported proposals, two clarification items, and no deadline or meeting proposal.

findings.criterion: Unproven provider reversal and elapsed continuity
findings.observation: The final local UI now directly proves speaker uncertainty, forwarded-source limits, unresolved identity persistence, temporal handle ordering, correction history, stale approval, source withdrawal and restore, and capture idempotency. No approved real-provider effect has been reversed through the UI, and no real elapsed cross-day return has been observed.
findings.evidence: The three remaining critical non-passes in docs/evaluations/2026-08-11-system-ui-click-acceptance-003.json are ACCESS-10, STATE-08, and ACTION-10; backend-built-r6 still records zero direct external writes.
findings.user_impact: Local governed state is materially safer, but provider lifecycle claims and next-day durability are not justified for sensitive paid use.
findings.recommendation: Use separately authorized provider-sandbox and next-day pilot runs; preserve approval, destination readback, reversal semantics, retention, deletion, and incident evidence.
findings.verification: The provider effect is at-most-once, observable, reversible where promised, and deletable, and the next-day UI reconstructs the same governed state without repair.

strengths: Unauthorized sources now disappear from evidence, proposals, actions, and current-state derivation, while unrelated authorized facts remain.
Restored evidence returns only to pending review; prior facts, approvals, and actions do not revive automatically.
Retry after a committed write preserves the original observation time and receipt, preventing silent duplicates.
Identity uncertainty, current-versus-historical ownership, wrong-person correction, stale approval, unknown effects, supersession, and deletion remain explicit and auditable.
missing_evidence: Production parity for temporal ambiguity and usable authenticated access.
A real provider sandbox lifecycle including approved effect reversal.
A real elapsed cross-day continuity trace.
vetoes: The deployed public Demo still converts unresolved relative time into confirmable deadline and meeting authority.
open_questions: Which release probe will fail deployment automatically when the public Demo regresses from clarification to action?
